known_training_manifests.note: the actual dataset run_tbg_registry_spectral_loss.py:split_paths() reads (DATASET = Comparison/datasets/tbg_md_plus_registry/n558); its train split has exactly 558 rows, matching training_plan.json:physical_train_samples=558 exactly (row-for-row: split_paths() computes physical_train_samples as len(train_paths) over this same manifest's train split). 474 of the 558 rows are MD-sourced (sample_id prefixed by their source MD stacking, not 'tbg_registry_grid_12x12__'); registry_mask in split_paths() identifies the other 84 as registry rows by the 'tbg_registry_grid_12x12__' sample_id prefix -- the same 84 rows already declared in the entry below via tbg_registry_grid_12x12/frozen_split_manifest.json, now doubly covered. Each MD row carries source_run/source_sample_id back to Comparison/datasets/tbg_pure_md_nested/n474 (itself traceable to Comparison/datasets/bilayer_graphene_{AA,AB,BA}_md200, which still holds raw MD_steps/md_temperature_blocks on disk) plus a full artifact_sha256 block (RUN.fdf, XV, HSX, TSHS, TSDE, ORB_INDX, STRUCT_OUT, metadata) per row.

matches training_plan.json:registry_samples=84; kept alongside the n558 manifest above as the original, narrower reference (the 84 rows it declares are a strict subset of the n558 manifest's 558 train rows)

checkpoint_lineage.structural_family_note: The checkpoint's known training/holdout data is lateral-registry-probe bilayer graphene (commensurate AA/AB/BA stacking grids, small unit cells) plus an MD component (bilayer graphene AA/AB/BA stacking, ~200-step trajectories at multiple temperature blocks; see Comparison/datasets/tbg_pure_md_nested/n474 and its source bilayer_graphene_{AA,AB,BA}_md200 datasets). The EPC evaluation structures are a pristine graphene primitive cell (2 atoms) and a rigid (31,30) magic-angle twisted-bilayer supercell (11164 atoms) -- a different structural family by atom count and stacking construction alone. audit_epc_lineage.py verifies this claim by geometry comparison rather than accepting this note as sufficient.
checkpoint_lineage.training_provenance_gap: Previously: training_plan.json declares physical_train_samples=558 drawn from MD trajectories, and no row-level manifest for that MD-sourced portion had been located. Resolved 2026-09-04: Comparison/datasets/tbg_md_plus_registry/n558/frozen_split_manifest.json is the exact dataset run_tbg_registry_spectral_loss.py:split_paths() reads to build train_paths (DATASET points at this directory); its train split has exactly 558 rows (474 MD-sourced + 84 registry-sourced, matching physical_train_samples=558/registry_samples=84 precisely), each with structure paths, artifact sha256 hashes and source_run/source_sample_id lineage back to the raw MD trajectory datasets, which are still present on disk. See known_training_manifests above.

upstream_checkpoint.relationship: spectral-best checkpoint is fine-tuned from this base checkpoint (training_plan.json:source_checkpoint); its own training lineage is not re-traced by this document and is declared unknown to audit_epc_lineage.py

frozen_before_commit.note: This document was authored at working-tree state descending from this commit. It consolidates protocol files that were themselves frozen (see each source_protocols[].sha256 and generated_at) at or before this commit, and it records the checkpoint/structure sha256 values it read at authoring time. Any later change to a referenced checkpoint, manifest or structure file will change its sha256 and audit_epc_lineage.py will report the reference as stale rather than silently re-trusting it.

holdout_semantics.calibration: may be inspected freely while setting tolerances; never itself a reported result
holdout_semantics.result: the pre-registered experiment; evaluated last and never used to set a tolerance
holdout_semantics.source: definitions as used verbatim in the per-protocol 'splits' blocks referenced below
holdout_semantics.validation: used once, after tolerances are frozen, to test whether they transfer; this and 'result' together are the holdout set

purpose: The scientific audit of E-F_001 found preregistration/holdout controls scattered across per-protocol JSON files with no single frozen declaration of the holdout set and no checkpoint-lineage record at all. This document consolidates the holdout declarations already frozen in Comparison/results/epc/preregistration/**/*.json (by reference and sha256, not by copying their content) and adds the checkpoint-lineage declaration those files were missing. It is the --preregistration input audit_epc_lineage.py reads.

validation.purpose: test whether the calibrated bound transfers to a direction and a k that took part in no fit. Used once, after the tolerances are frozen.
